speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Prime Minister regarding the Shared Responsibility Framework that was jointly proposed by MAS and IMDA on 25 October 2023, how does the "waterfall approach" on losses arising from phishing scams adequately safeguard consumers' interests.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Prime Minister whether the proposed framework for equitable sharing of losses between scam victims and financial institutions will consider (i) the better protection of some elderly scam victims through the use of physical hardware tokens for two-factor authentication rather than digital tokens and (ii) the number of elderly banking customers who have limited digital literacy and are placed in a potentially invidious position when their bank phased out the use of physical hardware tokens.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Under SRF, the FI stands at the top of this waterfall.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If the FI does not fulfil any of its four anti-scam duties, it will compensate the scam victim fully for the loss suffered, regardless of whether the telco has discharged its duties or the victim has taken the necessary precautions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Likewise, if the FI has fulfilled its duties but the telco has not, then the telco is expected to bear full responsibility for the loss.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Only if both the FI and telco have discharged their duties fully, will the customer, who stands at the bottom of the waterfall, have to bear the loss.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This approach recognises the key roles of FIs and telcos in preventing scams, and also reflects the SRF’s policy intent of strengthening their direct accountability to consumers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It incentivises FIs and telcos to strictly uphold the desired standards of anti-scam controls.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The duties defined for FIs in the SRF are built on a broader suite of measures that major retail banks are implementing to strengthen the security of digital banking in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We do not have data on the number of phishing scams that involve potential breaches of duties by FIs, but such data will be tracked under the SRF going forward.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Besides assigning accountability for scam losses, the important point is that full implementation by FIs and telcos of their respective safeguards should materially reduce the risk of phishing scams in this first instance.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The average loss per phishing scam has also declined by 20% over the same period.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Government will continue to monitor this closely.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are all committed to stem this rising tide of scams and losses.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng had asked if the SRF would consider seniors with limited digital literacy when their bank phased out the use of physical hardware tokens.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The retail banks already offer physical tokens for customers who request for them.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Separate from the SRF, MAS has asked the banks to assess and implement customer authentication mechanisms that are more resistant to both phishing and malware attacks.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: When these measures are well developed, we can consider them for inclusion into the SRF.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I covered these measures extensively in my response to the Adjournment Motion filed by Ms Lim in September.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) released a media statement on 24 October 2023 outlining banks' efforts to protect consumers against scams, including through anti-scam measures and also raising consumer awareness.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But SRF is not the only means through which scam victims can seek assistance.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As ABS announced, banks have discretionary goodwill payment frameworks for their scam victims beyond the SRF.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Depending on the circumstances of each scam case, the sophistication of the scam typology and the consumer's financial situation, banks have covered part or all of the losses incurred by scam victims.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS has leaned on the banks to be even more accommodative in applying their goodwill payment frameworks.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These goodwill frameworks complement the SRF, which is intended to strengthen the accountability of FIs and telcos to consumers when they have breached their defined duties.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have three supplementary questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I wonder if he will agree with me that the waterfall approach can actually be seen as giving the banks a free pass, if they are able to tick the four boxes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That means to say, if they fulfil the four prescribed duties that are in the paper, they will not have to bear any losses, and based on the case studies in the paper, it appears to be so.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I wonder whether he will agree with me that, in effect, this is what the waterfall approach will end up achieving for the banks.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question is: he mentioned that the four obligations set out in the paper are already being implemented by the banks.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, on the question of physical tokens, I have a Parliamentary Question No 44 on this topic, but I do not know why it was not grouped together.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And I myself went to a local bank to request a hardware token.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I was first told that it is not going to be issued.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And then, I had to insist and special approval was then obtained from the branch manager to issue the token to me.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I was also warned that it might be phased out in due course and they cannot assure me that this service would be available.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I wonder whether the Minister of State is aware of this as well.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, I want to thank Ms Sylvia Lim and Dr Tan Wu Meng for constantly working on this, together with MAS as well as the Government.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think it is an issue which we are incredibly concerned about and we are taking action.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If the Member might indulge me, I will first answer the third question.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: What we can do and what we will ask the banks to do in terms of the request for tokens, is to make it easier.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we take that feedback and we will put it back through MAS as well as the banks to ensure that customers who require physical tokens and are going to the banks to request for physical tokens, that process is made easier, particularly if they are not as adept or they do not yet have that confidence with digital tokens.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think that is a very important point, so, thank you for making that point.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We will look into it and we will ask the banks to smoothen this process out.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Member then also had two questions, with regard to the waterfall approach, as well as whether the banks are already fulfilling duties.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Given that the Member had talked about the approach by the UK, maybe I can draw a distinction between what the UK is doing and what we are doing.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There are, of course, variations between the UK's approach, as well as our approach, and let me go into detail why we have taken this approach.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First, the recent moves by the UK and Australia are not the norm globally; and, in fact, these approaches will evolve over time.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Singapore, like many jurisdictions, has adopted a slightly different approach on scams that are involving authorised transactions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Authorised transactions are scams, such as love, investment and job scams, for which the customer has authorised the transactions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If you think about the pre-digital banking days, the victims of such scams would have effectively just handed over cash, or written a cheque to these scammers promising a job or an investment return.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Now, they are making these transactions through digital means.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is challenging for a bank or telco if the SRF were to cover such scams – it would have to extend to all manner of deceptions, where victims are tricked into willingly handing over their money.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That is why for scams involving authorised transactions, in this case, the best approach – and, in fact, we are raising this awareness – is for customers to exercise utmost vigilance and take personal responsibility.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Therefore, we also stepping up public education efforts, including constant public advisories.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But as we had discussed in the Adjournment Motion, we also want to guard against the moral hazard risk, in terms of consumers letting their guard down and potentially also working in cahoots with scammers to defraud the banks.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Both the Member and I have heard feedback, even from the general public, that it would not be fair for the FIs, telcos and, ultimately, the wider group of customers who have exercised care, to have to bear the cost of compensating the scam losses from authorised transactions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Scams involving unauthorised transactions are, of course, fundamentally different.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The transfer takes place primarily without the victim's knowledge or consent.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That is why we place responsibility on the FIs at the top of the waterfall and the telcos at the second layer, to safeguard the consumer.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Therefore, the SRF is for phishing scams where the customer is tricked into disclosing his bank credentials and scammers are looking at unauthorised withdrawals.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I will also share a couple of things that are quite important.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This framework has to be seen in a broader scheme of things.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: What the banks have been doing – and in fact, MAS has been working very closely with them, together with the Cyber Security Agency (CSA), as well as the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) – are, and I think the Member would have seen them, some of the changes and developments since the Adjournment Motion.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First, MAS works very closely with the banks to implement and strengthen anti-scam controls.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Since we have discussed in our Adjournment Motion, four major retail banks have rolled out anti-malware controls.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I also talked earlier on about the goodwill payment frameworks.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS is leaning on the banks to be even more accommodative in applying these goodwill payment frameworks, taking into account the sophistication of scam typology, as well as consumers' financial situations, amongst others.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regards to the consultation paper, it is ongoing right now.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is from 25 October to 20 December.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We are asking six questions, including the questions the Member had asked about the waterfall approach, and about evolving scam typologies and the approaches to this.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, I encourage the Member to submit, and she can also directly send to me, her comments as well as reviews.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I can also confirm that my Clementi residents have great difficulty when they approach a bank trying to get a physical token.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I, myself, approached a bank as well and was told that the physical token had been phased out and it was not an option.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: So, it seems quite clear that there are a number of banks across Singapore who are making it very hard for customers to get a physical token – making it hard without fear or favour, possibly.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have three supplementary questions to the Minister.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The preliminary findings suggest these were phishing or malware scams.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: These residents did not ask to be transitioned to the OTP SMS or a digital token.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: They did not ask to have all their risks concentrated in a single device – their handphone.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: When MAS looks at existing cases, given the new framework, will the goodwill consideration by the banks take into account these new norms?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The second question is, we know that some smartphones already allow malware downloads much more easily than other smartphone operating systems.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: What is being done to ensure the smartphone manufacturers are awakened to this responsibility and do the right thing by customers?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Thirdly, Mr Speaker, if I can suggest a consumer protection perspective.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: If today, there was a consumer home appliance and a reasonable lay person could be tricked into using it the wrong way, causing injury or damage that will cost their life savings, we know what the consumer protection approach would be.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Will MAS consider this as well, especially given the clear and present concern that so many Clementi residents face?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to the goodwill payment as well as malware and also the consumer facing, please allow me to take a step back and share a few different perspectives.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The first is that if we think about this, the SRF, in its nature and if you compare what we are doing with what other jurisdictions are doing, we would be the first to look at it from an ecosystem perspective.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: That means, not just the FIs but now the telcos are involved in this waterfall approach, with the consumers being at the bottom of the waterfall but the FIs at the top of the waterfall.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Then, you will ask what happens then to other ecosystem players, such as the tech players?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The SRF consultation will look at both the wider ecosystem players eventually, because this is a live document and scam topologies will change over time; the approach towards addressing these will also change over time.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But for now, we are looking at FIs as well as telcos.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, it is a good start and it is a start that we will constantly review and refresh.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to these other ecosystem players, when we look at it, CSA and SPF have been working, in fact, with key tech players.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, Google has been working with IMDA, MAS and FIs to strengthen Android security to better detect malicious apps, for example.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The banks, as I mentioned earlier on, have money lock, they have prevented site loading as well, providing these friction measures.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, let us look at it in concert.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With regard to malware, we understand that malware is a rising concern.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I know that people have asked questions about why are malware scams excluded from this version of SRF.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, not just the Member's Clementi residents but I think many other residents have also experienced malware scams, including many family members as well.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For now, the duties that are identified for this version of the SRF work well to address phishing scams.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, the consultation paper also provides for that as one of the six questions.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And I hope that both Members and other Members as well as members of the public will give us your full support and your full ideas so that we can refine and expand if necessary.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Speaker, two further questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier, the Minister of State mentioned that SRF, as proposed by MAS, covers only unauthorised transactions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Does he agree with me that even accepting that premise, so long as the banks fulfil the four obligations defined in the paper, even if the bank was negligent in some other way, the bank can actually push the liability down the waterfall?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And, in fact, they will and have implemented a goodwill payment framework.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will lean in on the banks to tilt the balance towards the banks offering more of these goodwill payment frameworks.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, if the consumer himself has faced a particular financial hardship, then the banks will take all of these into account when deciding whether to issue a goodwill payment to the consumer.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng, last supplementary question from you, please.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I have raised previously in this House the idea of forced vs unforced errors, especially given the emergence of new scams, such as deep fakes, where a bank can be masqueraded in a way that seems very authentic.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Can I ask the Minister of State, in this framework, if someone has been tricked by a deep fake scam or a scam that seems so authentic that a reasonable person would be at significant risk of being tricked, would that be an authorised transaction and would it be subject to support and compensation under the waterfall system?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: If it is found that the telco has to bear, the telco will bear.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And then, finally, again, as I mentioned in my reply to Ms Sylvia Lim, if it appears that the consumer has also fulfilled his responsibility, then the banks themselves will look into the specific circumstances to issue these goodwill payments.
